program.source: export function evaluate({ inputs, time, seed, state }) { const launchSpeed = inputs.launchSpeed; const gravity = 9.8; const t = time; const height = launchSpeed * t - (gravity * t * t) / 2; const velocity = launchSpeed - gravity * t; const apexTime = launchSpeed / gravity; const apexHeight = (launchSpeed * launchSpeed) / (2 * gravity); const scaleY = 30; const baseY = 360; const ballY = baseY - height * scaleY; const ballX = 320; let motionState = "Moving up"; if (Math.abs(velocity) < 0.05) { motionState = "Still for an instant"; } else if (velocity < 0) { motionState = "Moving down"; } const gravityState = "Gravity pulls down"; const objects = []; objects.push(sdk.panel({ x: 40, y: 40, w: 560, h: 360, title: "Vertical Motion", state: motionState, id: "lane.toss" })); objects.push(sdk.axis("axis.height", { x: 100, y: 360, length: 300, orientation: "y", min: 0, max: 2.5, ticks: [0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5], label: "Height", unit: "m" })); objects.push(sdk.line("guide.launch", 80, baseY, 560, baseY, { role: "neutral", opacity: 0.5 })); objects.push(sdk.circle("ball.toss", ballX, ballY, 28, { role: "output" })); if (Math.abs(velocity) >= 0.05) { const vDir = velocity > 0 ? "up" : "down"; objects.push(sdk.vector("vec.v", { x: ballX + 24, y: ballY }, { value: Math.abs(velocity), direction: vDir }, { scale: 15, minLength: 12, label: "v" })); } objects.push(sdk.vector("vec.a", { x: ballX - 24, y: ballY }, { value: 9.8, direction: "down" }, { scale: 5, minLength: 12, label: "a" })); const calloutLines = [motionState, gravityState]; objects.push(sdk.callout(ballX + 45, ballY - 20, calloutLines, { id: "callout.toss" })); return { frame: { width: 640, height: 420, objects: objects, readouts: [{ id: "motionState", value: motionState }, { id: "gravityState", value: gravityState }] }, quantities: { launchSpeed: launchSpeed, gravity: gravity, apexTime: apexTime, apexHeight: apexHeight, velocity: velocity, height: height } }; }

manifest.title: The ball stops rising. Gravity doesn’t stop.
manifest.summary: Gravity slows the ball on the way up and speeds it up on the way down. At the top, the ball is still for an instant while gravity pulls it downward.
manifest.description: A ball moves vertically along a height scale. A blue motion arrow shows its velocity, shortening as it rises, disappearing at the apex, and pointing downward as it falls. A dashed warm gravity arrow points downward constantly. A callout next to the ball reports its motion state.
assumptions: Gravity fixed at 9.8 m/s^2, no air resistance, up is positive.
manifest.instructions: Change launch speed, then press Play. At the top, playback pauses so you can inspect the arrows. Press Play again to watch the ball fall, or drag the timeline to inspect any moment.
